spans.s:
√muṣ (muṣṇā́ti; mumóṣa; ámoṣīt; muṣitá;
muṣitvā́; -múṣya). rob; steal. [cf.
mū́ṣ, ‘the thief, i. e. mouse’; μῦς, ‘mouse,’
and from the shape, ‘muscle’; Lat. mūs,
‘mouse,’ whence diminutive mus-culus,
‘muscle’; AS. mūs, ‘mouse’ and ‘muscle,’
Eng. mouse; Ger. Maus, ‘mouse’ (whence
denom. mausen, ‘steal,’ in which we are
brought back again to the orig. mg of
the primitive), and also ‘muscle of the
thumb’; further, μυῖα, *μυσια, Lat. mus-ca,
‘fly’: see also muṣka.]

mū́ṣ, m. f. mouse. [‘the thief,’ √muṣ,
q. v.: see 383a^2.]

muṣká, m.
 —1. testicle;
 —2. pudenda
muliebria. [from noun muṣ, i. e. (383a^2)
mū́ṣ, ‘mouse’: for mgs, see under √muṣ:
cf. μύσ-χον• τὸ ἀνδρεῖον καὶ γυναικεῖον μόριον:
w. muṣka, cf. also Persian mushk, Eng.
musk, ‘perfume got from a bag behind
the navel of the musk-deer.’]

muṣka-deśa, m. region of the testes,
groin.

mūṣaka, m. thief; mouse, 46^17; Mousey,
as name of a man, 47^21. [√muṣ, q. v.]
mūṣika, m. mouse, rat. [√muṣ, q. v.]

mūṣika-nirviśeṣa, a. undistinguished
from a mouse.
